documents.title: Your first capture
documents.summary: The simulator camera sim:0 lets you try every command without hardware.
documents.body: Start here Your first capture The simulator camera sim:0 lets you try every command without hardware. Install Capturefab . Open a terminal and run the commands below one at a time. Then replace sim:0 with an ID from capturefab list . capturefab list --kind sim capturefab info -c sim:0 capturefab capture -c sim:0 -o 'first-{seq}.png' capturefab inspect -c sim:0 capturefab set -c sim:0 exposure=5ms gain=3 capturefab record -c sim:0 -o clip.mp4 --for 10s info shows the image size, pixel format, exposure, gain, trigger and the controls the camera has. capture saves first-0001.png ; run it again for first-0002.png , because Capturefab never overwrites a file. inspect measures brightness, clipping and sharpness and writes a small preview image. set changes several values as one change. record saves ten seconds of H.264 video. Add --json to any command for one JSON document on stdout. Each command lists its options and examples with --help .

documents.title: Use Capturefab from an AI agent
documents.summary: Coding agents such as Claude Code or Codex drive cameras through the CLI and read its JSON results.
documents.body: Start here Use Capturefab from an AI agent Coding agents such as Claude Code or Codex drive cameras through the CLI and read its JSON results. Install Capturefab where the agent runs, so capturefab is on its PATH . Give the agent agents.md , or tell it to run capturefab schema first. Allow the commands it may run without asking, by prefix (see below). Start with a bounded task on sim:0 , then name the real camera. capturefab schema capturefab schema capture capturefab list --json capturefab inspect --json -c sim:0 --preview none capturefab capture --json -c sim:0 -o 'shots/{seq}.png' Every command takes --json and prints exactly one JSON document. The exit code gives the category and error.code the reason, so an agent knows what to do next without reading prose. schema describes every command in about 8 KB (roughly 2,500 tokens). Flags can follow the command, so a harness can allow commands by their first words. Command effects, from capturefab schema Effect Examples Suggested permission read list , info , features , get , inspect , jobs , doctor , schema Allow file_write capture , record , preset save Allow in the task's folder camera_write set , auto , preset apply , jobs stop Allow for the task's cameras disruptive exec , session start , session stop , serve , debug write Ask first The effect is for a command without these flags: --set on inspect , capture and record , and --auto on capture and record , change camera settings and leave them changed, and network --tune writes camera network settings. A prefix also matches every subcommand: a rule for capturefab jobs allows capturefab jobs stop all . Allow exact prefixes such as capturefab jobs list and capturefab jobs wait , and have the agent ask before a call with --set , --auto or --tune on a camera the task does not own. inspect writes its preview into a private folder: capturefab --json doctor names it in dirs.inspect . Let the agent read files there, or pass --preview none or --preview PATH . Your harness decides whether the model sees images. --keep 5m keeps a camera open between calls, which makes measuring loops fast.

documents.title: Install and verify
documents.summary: One command picks the build for this computer, checks its SHA-256 and installs capturefab for your account.
documents.body: Start here Install and verify One command picks the build for this computer, checks its SHA-256 and installs capturefab for your account. # macOS and Linux: ~/.local/share/capturefab, with the command in ~/.local/bin curl -fsSL https://capturefab.com/install.sh | sh # Windows PowerShell: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Capturefab, on your user PATH irm https://capturefab.com/install.ps1 | iex The installers never use sudo or administrator rights. To read the script first: curl -fsSLO https://capturefab.com/install.sh; less install.sh; sh install.sh . --dry-run prints the file, URL and checksum it would use; --prefix DIR and --bin-dir DIR choose other folders. To download by hand, open the download page . Select the build for your installed operating system and processor: Apple silicon uses ARM64, Intel and AMD PCs usually use x64. Check the file in the download's folder: # Linux echo "EXPECTED_SHA256 DOWNLOADED_FILE" | sha256sum -c # macOS echo "EXPECTED_SHA256 DOWNLOADED_FILE" | shasum -a 256 -c # Windows PowerShell if ((Get-FileHash .\DOWNLOADED_FILE -Algorithm SHA256).Hash -eq 'EXPECTED_SHA256') { 'OK: checksum matches' } else { 'MISMATCH: do not open this file' } Linux and macOS print OK for a match; anything else means do not use the file. Then extract the archive. It holds the capturefab executable ( capturefab.exe on Windows), a README and the license files. Put capturefab on your PATH The installers already do this. After a manual download, put the executable in a folder on your PATH : # macOS and Linux, from the extracted folder install -Dm755 ./capturefab ~/.local/bin/capturefab # Linux mkdir -p ~/.local/bin && cp ./capturefab ~/.local/bin/ # macOS # Windows PowerShell, from the extracted folder $dir = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\Capturefab" New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $dir | Out-Null; Copy-Item -Recurse -Force .\* $dir $path = (Get-Item HKCU:\Environment).GetValue('Path', '', 'DoNotExpandEnvironmentNames') New-ItemProperty HKCU:\Environment Path -PropertyType ExpandString -Value "$path;$dir" -Force | Out-Null Open a new terminal and run capturefab --version . If it is not found on macOS or Linux, add export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" to ~/.zshrc or ~/.profile . First use: system prompts The first camera or network command can make your system ask for permission. These answers decide whether cameras appear. Prompts on first use System What to expect macOS macOS asks for Camera and Local Network access for the app you run the command in, such as Terminal, iTerm or your editor. Allow both: webcams need Camera, and GigE Vision, ONVIF and RTSP discovery need Local Network. To change them later, open System Settings › Privacy & Security › Camera or Local Network and turn that app on. A download from a browser is checked online by Gatekeeper the first time it runs. Windows A build marked Unsigned on the download page can show Windows protected your PC from SmartScreen. Check the SHA-256 first, then choose More info → Run anyway , or run Unblock-File .\capturefab.exe . The PowerShell installer needs neither. When Windows Defender Firewall asks, allow Capturefab on Private networks . GigE Vision and RTSP-over-UDP video arrive as inbound UDP; blocking it shows up as stream timeouts. USB3 Vision needs WinUSB. The camera's USB3 Vision interface must use the WinUSB driver. Close vendor camera software first. Use the vendor's driver tool if it can switch the camera to WinUSB; otherwise run Zadig , choose Options › List All Devices , select the camera's interface, choose WinUSB and select Replace Driver . Vendor software that needs its own driver cannot open the camera until you roll the driver back in Device Manager. Linux There are no prompts, but USB3 Vision cameras need device permissions and GigE Vision needs a larger socket receive buffer. Run capturefab doctor : it checks both and prints the command for each fix. The line computer guide explains the udev rule and net.core.rmem_max . Minimum operating system versions Build Minimum requirement macOS ARM64 macOS 11.0 macOS x64 macOS 10.15 Windows x64 Windows 10; Windows 11 on ARM can use x64 emulation. Windows ARM64 Windows 11 on ARM Linux x64 and ARM64 glibc 2.28; examples include Debian 10, RHEL 8 and Jetson Linux R34. These minimums also apply to the included FFmpeg executable. Windows builds need no Visual C++ redistributable. There is no 32-bit ARM build: on Debian-based Linux, dpkg --print-architecture must print arm64 for the ARM64 build. Release builds need no separate Aravis, FFmpeg, libusb or vendor SDK. capturefab --version capturefab doctor # Optional: verify GitHub build provenance gh attestation verify DOWNLOADED_FILE --repo capturefab/capturefab

documents.title: Upgrade from the desktop app
documents.summary: Capturefab is now a command-line tool. Releases up to 0.5.0 were a desktop app with a CLI inside.
documents.body: Start here Upgrade from the desktop app Capturefab is now a command-line tool. Releases up to 0.5.0 were a desktop app with a CLI inside. The desktop window, browser client, built-in AI assistant, datasets, camera hubs, document scanners, workflow files and update checks are gone. Cameras, captures, recordings and saved sign-ins work as before through the commands on this page, with new names and a new JSON contract: read the command reference before you reuse a script. macOS: run the install script. It replaces a ~/.local/bin/capturefab link into Capturefab.app and says what it changed; the app itself stays until you delete it. If your shell profile adds /Applications/Capturefab.app/Contents/MacOS to PATH , remove that line. Linux: the install script removes the launcher entry and icons an earlier install added. Earlier versions stay in ~/.local/share/capturefab until you delete them. Windows: the install script removes the Start menu shortcut an earlier install added and keeps one Capturefab folder on your PATH . Files the desktop app kept, such as its preferences, saved hubs, destinations and dataset files, are not read any more; delete them when you no longer need them. Saved camera sign-ins stay in the OS credential store and keep working. To keep using the desktop app, keep version 0.5.0 and skip the update it offers; its downloads remain at https://capturefab.com/download/v0.5.0/ , with each file listed in releases.json .

documents.title: Find cameras
documents.summary: list searches every transport at once and prints an ID for each camera.
documents.body: Cameras Find cameras list searches every transport at once and prints an ID for each camera. capturefab list capturefab list --kind gige,u3v --timeout 3s capturefab list --kind webcam capturefab --json list Kinds are gige , u3v , webcam , onvif , screen and sim . Screen captures and simulators appear only when --kind names them. --timeout sets how long GigE and ONVIF broadcasts collect answers (default 1s ). A transport that cannot be searched adds a line to warnings instead of failing the command. Pass an ID to -c . A unique serial number or a GigE IPv4 address also works. Without -c , a command uses the only camera a session holds, or else the only camera list finds; with several it exits 2 with camera_ambiguous and lists the candidates, except at a terminal without --json , where it shows a numbered list and asks which (Enter takes the first). CAPTUREFAB_CAMERA sets a default. A GigE camera needs a reachable address on a wired adapter's subnet; capturefab network checks the path. USB3 Vision needs operating system access: the udev rule on Linux, an available IOKit interface on macOS and WinUSB on Windows. Read the camera requirements and limits .

documents.title: Camera selectors
documents.summary: -c takes a list ID, a serial, an IP address, a stream URL, a file or a simulator.
documents.body: Cameras Camera selectors -c takes a list ID, a serial, an IP address, a stream URL, a file or a simulator. Selector examples Source Selector GigE Vision or USB3 Vision camera gige:00c0df123456 , a u3v: ID, a serial number or 192.168.1.20 Webcam or capture card avfoundation:Camera Name (macOS), v4l2:/dev/video0 (Linux), dshow:video=Camera Name (Windows); add ?size=1280x720&fps=30 to ask for a mode Network stream rtsp://cam.local/stream , rtsps://… , srt://… , http(s)://… ONVIF camera onvif://cam.local or onvif:http://HOST/onvif/device_service Video or image file a path, such as clip.mkv Simulator sim:0 , sim:1 , sim:line , sim:depth , sim:microscope , sim:thermal , sim:replay:PATH Quote selectors with spaces, ? or & in a shell. Never put a password in a selector you save in a script; save it with login add instead. Credentials in URLs are always redacted in output. capturefab capture -c 'avfoundation:Camera Name?size=1280x720' -o webcam.png capturefab features -c v4l2:/dev/video0 VideoMode capturefab capture -c rtsp://cam.local/stream -n 5 -o snapshots/ capturefab capture -c clip.mkv -n 100 -o frames/

documents.title: Simulated cameras
documents.summary: Built-in cameras for learning, scripting and tests without hardware.
documents.body: Cameras Simulated cameras Built-in cameras for learning, scripting and tests without hardware. sim:0 (and sim:1 , sim:2 , …) is a moving pattern camera with exposure, gain, frame rate, region, pixel formats (Mono8, Mono12, Mono12p, Mono14p, Mono16, RGB8, RGB12, BayerRG8, BayerRG12, BayerRG12p), auto exposure and a trigger bank. sim:line , sim:depth , sim:microscope and sim:thermal act like those kinds of camera. sim:replay:PATH replays a video, an image or a folder of them. capturefab inspect -c sim:0 --set exposure=40ms capturefab capture -c sim:0 -c sim:1 -o 'multi/{camera}-{seq}.png' capturefab capture -c sim:replay:/data/clip.mp4 -n 100 -o replay-frames/ A simulator keeps the settings you give it until its runtime folder is cleared, as a real camera keeps its own until it powers off, and commands keep it open for 60 seconds between them. capture --set changes settings and captures in one call. Read the simulated camera guide for replay rules.

documents.title: Read and change settings
documents.summary: info summarizes a camera; get and set read and write features and controls in one call.
documents.body: Cameras Read and change settings info summarizes a camera; get and set read and write features and controls in one call. capturefab info -c sim:0 capturefab features -c sim:0 Trigger capturefab features -c sim:0 'Exposure*' --all capturefab get -c sim:0 exposure gain ExposureTime 'TriggerMode[FrameStart]' capturefab set -c sim:0 exposure=5ms gain=3 capturefab set -c sim:0 roi=0,0,320,240 fps=20 --dry-run capturefab exec -c sim:0 'TriggerSoftware[FrameStart]' Names are the camera's GenICam features ( ExposureTime ), a feature at a selector value ( TriggerMode[FrameStart] , or Feature[Selector=Value] ; quote these in the shell, because zsh expands brackets), or a portable control: exposure , gain , fps , roi ( x,y,w,h or full ), format , trigger ( off , software , line0:rising …), auto_exposure and auto_wb . Time features take durations: ExposureTime=10ms . set writes every value as one change, in an order that keeps the camera valid: offsets before sizes, an auto mode off before its value, a lower frame rate before a longer exposure. If a write fails, every value written is put back, and so is the rest of the image geometry a write moved (a binning rescales the size and offsets); the error's details.rollback lists what was restored. --dry-run checks the values against the camera and shows the writes in order. The result lists each changed value as read back, which can be rounded to the camera's increment. A wrong name exits 2 with feature_not_found and close names in details.did_you_mean ; a value outside the range exits 2 with out_of_range and details.nearest . features shows the common features by default; a pattern, --category or --all searches every level. exec runs a command feature, such as UserSetSave[UserSet1] to keep settings in the camera.

documents.title: Measure exposure and focus
documents.summary: inspect measures a fresh frame and writes a small preview, without saving a capture.
documents.body: Cameras Measure exposure and focus inspect measures a fresh frame and writes a small preview, without saving a capture. capturefab inspect -c sim:0 capturefab inspect -c sim:0 --set exposure=20ms --region 0.25,0.25,0.5,0.5 capturefab inspect -c sim:0 --keep 5m --preview none capturefab --json inspect -c sim:0 -v --preview none capturefab watch -c sim:0 --show The result gives brightness as fractions of full scale ( mean , p1 , p50 , p99 ), the shares and counts of pixels at black and full scale ( clipped_low , clipped_high , clipped_low_px , clipped_high_px ), counted over every pixel at the frame's own bit depth, a verdict list of one or more of ok , dark , bright , clipped_high , clipped_low , not_settled and not_measured (such as ["ok"] or ["clipped_high","bright"] ; the frame is fine when it is exactly ["ok"] ) and, when exposure is off, suggest : how many stops to move and the exposure to try. focus.sharpness is the variance of the Laplacian; compare it between frames of one camera and scene. -v adds a 16-bin histogram, color channels and the Tenengrad, Brenner and variance focus measures. --set changes settings first, as set does, then measures a frame taken after the change. --region X,Y,W,H measures part of the frame, in fractions 0 to 1. The preview is a JPEG (longest edge --size , default 768) in a private folder that doctor names; --preview PATH writes it elsewhere and --preview none skips it. For a focus or aiming loop, the camera stays open between calls (60 seconds, or --keep 5m ), and --for 10s --every 200ms measures a series and returns the sharpest frame's measurements and preview. The measured frame is always one exposed after the camera's last settings change; --fresh N lets N more pass. A camera that sets its own exposure (a webcam, a stream, ExposureAuto=Continuous ) gets up to --warmup (default 2s ) to settle after it starts; not_settled in the verdict says it had not. --clip-threshold sets the share of pixels at full scale that makes the verdict clipped_high . watch measures continuously instead: in a terminal it redraws the measurements in place, and with --show the frame under them; otherwise, as with --json , it prints one JSON line per measurement ( --every , --for ).

documents.title: Auto exposure
documents.summary: auto settles exposure and gain, then holds them.
documents.body: Cameras Auto exposure auto settles exposure and gain, then holds them. capturefab auto -c sim:0 capturefab auto -c sim:0 --timeout 10s capturefab auto -c sim:0 --off capturefab capture -c sim:0 --auto -o settled.png auto uses the camera's own auto exposure once when it has one, and otherwise adjusts exposure and gain itself until the brightness settles or --timeout ends. The result reports settled , the exposure and gain it holds, and limited_by when a limit stopped it; settled: false still exits 0. --off turns the camera's auto exposure, gain and white balance off and keeps their values. --continuous leaves the camera's continuous auto exposure on; for cameras without one, Capturefab's own loop runs only in a session. Cameras without exposure control, such as thermal and line scan sources, exit 5 unsupported .

documents.title: Triggered capture
documents.summary: With a software trigger, capture fires it; with a hardware trigger, it waits for the line.
documents.body: Cameras Triggered capture With a software trigger, capture fires it; with a hardware trigger, it waits for the line. capturefab capture -c sim:0 --set trigger=software -o part.png capturefab set -c sim:0 trigger=line0:rising --keep 5m capturefab capture -c sim:0 -o 'part-{seq}.png' --timeout 30s capturefab capture -c sim:0 -n 1000 -o 'station/{time}.png' --timeout none --background capturefab jobs stop all capturefab set -c sim:0 trigger=off The trigger control sets TriggerMode , TriggerSource and TriggerActivation of the frame-start trigger together. A hardware-triggered capture waits up to --timeout for each frame (default 5s ); expiry exits 4 with trigger_timeout and the trigger configuration in error.details.trigger . --timeout none waits until the capture is stopped, and inspect --timeout none waits for its triggered frame the same way. Run a long triggered capture with --background and watch it with jobs . The trigger setting stays for the captures that follow: a camera keeps its settings, and a simulator or webcam keeps the ones Capturefab emulates for it until its runtime folder is cleared.

documents.title: Capture images
documents.summary: capture saves one frame, a burst, a time lapse or a delayed capture, and never overwrites a file.
documents.body: Capture & record Capture images capture saves one frame, a burst, a time lapse or a delayed capture, and never overwrites a file. capturefab capture -c sim:0 -o shot.png capturefab capture -c sim:0 -n 10 -o frames/ capturefab capture -c sim:0 -o shot.jpg --quality 85 capturefab capture -c sim:0 -o frames/ -f raw capturefab capture -c sim:0 --set exposure=20ms --set gain=6 -o bright.png capturefab capture -c sim:0 -o - > frame.png capturefab capture -c sim:0 -o shot2.png --dry-run Image formats Format Use png The default: lossless; 16-bit gray for monochrome frames wider than 8 bits (Mono10 to Mono16, packed or not), 8-bit gray for other monochrome, 8-bit RGB for color and Bayer. Carries tags and camera settings in its metadata. jpg Smaller files; --quality 1–100, default 90. Carries tags and camera settings. A Motion JPEG webcam, stream or file gives the JPEG it sent, as it was, at its own quality, and the result says "passthrough": true ; --quality encodes the frame again. raw The frame's bytes exactly as the camera sent them, at full bit depth: Bayer data, depth and thermal samples, and for webcams, streams and files the format FFmpeg decodes them to (gray, YUV or RGB). A NAME.json sidecar names the pixel format, its PFNC code, the size and the row length. Every common PFNC pixel format converts (see the pixel format table ). The result reports bit_depth , and source_bits when the file keeps fewer bits than the frame, such as a 12-bit Bayer frame saved as 8-bit PNG or JPEG. The format comes from the -o extension; -f chooses it when the name has none. A folder (existing, or ending in / ) gets names like {camera}-{time}-{seq}.png . Without -o , files go to the current folder. -o - writes one image to stdout; with --json the result then goes to stderr. --timeout is how long to wait for each frame (default 5s ). --set and --auto change the camera first. A file name that exists exits 1 with exists ; add {seq} or pass --on-exists number . Repeat -c to capture from several cameras at once: each is armed first, then all are asked for a frame at the same moment; the JSON result holds cameras , one entry each, and skew_ms , how far apart their first frames arrived. GigE cameras that share a network adapter are paced to a share of it ( bandwidth_mbps ). Ctrl-C stops a capture with exit 130, and error.details.files lists what was saved. capturefab capture -c sim:0 -o shot.png --inspect --manifest shots.jsonl capturefab capture -c sim:0 --set exposure=20ms --fresh 2 -o after.png capturefab capture -c sim:0 -n 100 -o 'scratch/{seq}.raw' --sync none The result says which frame each capture is: time (RFC 3339) and device_ts_ns , the camera's own clock where it has one. frames counts the frames the camera delivered while the capture ran, dropped those lost, and incomplete and resent what the transport received incomplete or asked for again, where it counts them; a burst adds fps , first_id , last_id , gaps and consecutive . The first frame saved is always one exposed after the camera's last settings change ( after_change when frames were let pass for it), and --fresh N lets N more pass. A camera that sets its own exposure gets up to --warmup (default 2s ) to settle after it starts: warmup_ms says how long it took, and settled: false with a warning that it had not. --inspect measures the last frame as inspect does, in the result's inspect block. --manifest FILE appends one JSON line per saved file with its path, time, size, SHA-256, settings and tags. Each file reaches the disk before it is reported; --sync none skips that for scratch captures a power cut may lose.

documents.title: Name files and tag captures
documents.summary: Templates in -o build file names from the camera, time, sequence and your tags.
documents.body: Capture & record Name files and tag captures Templates in -o build file names from the camera, time, sequence and your tags. capturefab capture -c sim:0 -n 10 -o 'parts/{date}/{tag:part}-{seq:4}.png' --tag part=A-100 --tag station=3 capturefab capture -c sim:0 -o 'labels/{tag:label}/{seq:5}.png' --tag label=defect capturefab capture -c sim:0 -o shot.png --on-exists number Output placeholders Placeholder Value {camera} The camera's model and serial, safe for file names {serial} The serial number {seq} , {seq:N} 1, 2, 3 …, padded to N digits (4 by default) {time} The time, such as 20261031-142233.123 {date} The date, such as 2026-10-31 {tag:KEY} The value of --tag KEY=VALUE {ext} png , jpg or raw Tags also go into each PNG and JPEG with the camera's settings. Paths are resolved against the folder you run the command in, also when a session does the work. Capturefab never overwrites a file: with {seq} it takes the next free number, and --on-exists number adds -0001 , -0002 … to a fixed name. Read the plant-floor guide for naming that analysis tools can read.

documents.title: Time lapses and delayed captures
documents.summary: --every spaces frames, --for or -n bounds them, and --at or --in delays the start.
documents.body: Capture & record Time lapses and delayed captures --every spaces frames, --for or -n bounds them, and --at or --in delays the start. capturefab capture -c sim:0 --every 10s --for 1h -o 'lapse/{seq}.jpg' --background capturefab capture -c sim:0 -n 100 --every 2s -o 'lapse/{seq:5}.png' capturefab capture -c sim:0 --at 06:00 -o morning.png capturefab capture -c sim:0 --in 5m -o later.png capturefab jobs capturefab jobs wait auto-1 --timeout 10m capturefab jobs stop all Durations need a unit: 250ms , 2s , 5m , 1h30m . --at takes HH:MM[:SS] in local time or an RFC 3339 time. Without --background the command runs until the series ends; with it, a session runs the job and the command returns its ID at once. See sessions and jobs .

documents.title: Record and stream video
documents.summary: record writes video to a file or streams it to a server through the bundled FFmpeg.
documents.body: Capture & record Record and stream video record writes video to a file or streams it to a server through the bundled FFmpeg. capturefab record -c sim:0 -o clip.mp4 --for 30s capturefab record -c sim:0 -o clip.mkv --codec ffv1 --for 5m capturefab record -c sim:0 -o clip.mp4 --bitrate 4M --max-size 2G capturefab record -c sim:0 -o rtsp://localhost:8554/cam --background capturefab record -c sim:0 -o 'srt://localhost:8890?streamid=publish:cam' --for 10m Files can be .mkv , .mp4 , .mov , .ts or .webm , and must not exist. Streams go to rtsp:// , srt:// , rtmp:// or udp:// receivers such as MediaMTX. --codec h264 (the default) uses a hardware encoder where one works and libx264 otherwise; hevc and av1 need a hardware encoder, unless the source is copied (below), and exit 5 before recording without one; ffv1 is lossless, in .mkv , and stores a Bayer camera's mosaic itself as gray samples. An H.264 or HEVC stream, video file or webcam mode is recorded as it arrives, without decoding or re-encoding its video: the result says "encoder":"copy" and the source's codec . The file starts at the source's last key frame, so it can begin up to one key-frame interval before the command. --codec naming another codec, --fps or --bitrate encodes instead. Windows always encodes. The source is still decoded while it is copied, for captures and inspection. Recording runs until --for ends, --max-size is reached or you press Ctrl-C, which is a normal end. The result reports frames , dropped , fps_actual , the codec and encoder used, why it ended and whether the file was finalized . --fps sets the frame rate written (default: the camera's).

documents.title: Save and restore settings
documents.summary: A preset keeps a camera's settings on this computer and restores them as one change.
documents.body: Capture & record Save and restore settings A preset keeps a camera's settings on this computer and restores them as one change. capturefab preset save bench -c sim:0 --note 'ring light 60%' capturefab preset list capturefab preset apply bench -c sim:0 --dry-run capturefab preset apply bench -c sim:0 capturefab preset export bench -o bench.json capturefab preset import bench.json --name bench2 apply writes every saved value as one change and puts every value back if one fails. --dry-run shows what would change, with disruptive changes (triggering, I/O lines, acquisition rate) marked. --strict changes nothing when a saved value does not fit the camera. --allow-other-model applies the settings two models share. --persist then saves the result in the camera's user set and makes it the power-on default. A preset lives on this computer; a user set lives in the camera.

documents.title: Password-protected cameras
documents.summary: login add saves a stream's user name and password in the OS credential store.
documents.body: Capture & record Password-protected cameras login add saves a stream's user name and password in the OS credential store. printf '%s\n' "$PASSWORD" | capturefab login add rtsp://cam.local/stream --user admin --password-stdin capturefab login list capturefab onvif resolve cam.local capturefab login rm rtsp://cam.local/stream login add connects once and saves the sign-in only if the camera accepts it ( --no-check skips that). The password comes from --password-stdin or CAPTUREFAB_CAMERA_PASSWORD , never the command line. Every later command for that address uses it. A camera that asks for a sign-in exits 3 with auth_required , and one that refuses it with auth_rejected . FFmpeg takes RTSP credentials only in its input URL, so other local users can read them in its command line. Plain RTSP Basic authentication and ONVIF over http:// send the password readably over the network; prefer rtsps:// , Digest authentication and fixed addresses on trusted networks. onvif resolve lists an ONVIF camera's profiles and RTSP streams.

documents.title: Sessions, --keep and jobs
documents.summary: A session keeps cameras open between commands and runs background jobs.
documents.body: Automate Sessions, --keep and jobs A session keeps cameras open between commands and runs background jobs. capturefab inspect -c sim:0 --keep 5m capturefab session start --name bench -c sim:0 --live capturefab session status bench capturefab capture -c sim:0 --every 10s --for 1h -o 'lapse/{seq}.jpg' --background capturefab jobs capturefab session stop bench capturefab serve --name line1 -c sim:0 --live Each camera runs in a worker process of its own. Every camera command keeps its camera warm: it starts or reuses a session named auto that holds the camera until it has been unused for 60 seconds, so the next commands skip connecting. --keep DUR holds it longer; --keep 0 , CAPTUREFAB_KEEP=0 or --no-session open and close the camera in the command alone, as on a computer without a writable runtime folder. Results are the same either way. session start starts a named session in the background that ends after --idle unused (default 30m ); serve runs one in the foreground with no idle limit, for systemd. --live keeps the cameras streaming, so captures take the newest frame at once. A command uses a session that holds its camera on its own. --session NAME picks one (also CAPTUREFAB_SESSION ), and --no-session never uses one. A camera another process holds exits 3 with camera_busy , naming the holder. capturefab shell -c CAM runs many commands with the cameras kept connected: a prompt with history and Tab completion in a terminal, or one command per line of stdin (or -e ) with one result per line. --background on capture or record returns a job: jobs lists every session's jobs, jobs wait ID exits 0 when the job is done (4 while it still runs) and jobs stop ID ends it, keeping the files. A job is armed , running or stopping , then done , failed , cancelled or interrupted ; the jobs of a session that died are listed as lost . session status lists each camera's state, frame counts and jobs, and for a camera whose worker exited, an error ( worker_crashed with its exit status and the last lines it wrote); the next command on that camera starts another worker. debug rpc sends one session command, a JSON object on stdin such as {"op":"status"} , {"op":"jobs"} , {"op":"wait","job":"auto-1","timeout_ms":5000} or {"op":"stop_job","job":"auto-1"} , and prints its reply; it is for debugging, and its commands can change between releases. The line computer guide runs a session at boot.

documents.title: GigE network checks
documents.summary: network checks how each GigE camera is reached; --tune shares bandwidth between cameras.
documents.body: Automate GigE network checks network checks how each GigE camera is reached; --tune shares bandwidth between cameras. capturefab network capturefab network --tune -c gige:00c0df123456 -c gige:00c0df654321 network lists the IPv4 adapters with their MTU and link speed, and each GigE camera found with the adapter that reaches it and a health summary. It changes nothing. --tune sets packet delay or throughput limits on the named cameras so they share a link without losing packets; they keep the setting until they power off. Host addresses, routes and MTUs are never changed. Give camera networks their own wired adapter where you can, and on Linux raise net.core.rmem_max as doctor suggests.

documents.title: Check this computer
documents.summary: doctor prints one line per check, with a copyable fix under each warning.
documents.body: Reference Check this computer doctor prints one line per check, with a copyable fix under each warning. capturefab doctor capturefab --json doctor The checks cover the bundled FFmpeg (webcams, streams, files and recording need it), the folders Capturefab uses, wired adapters for GigE Vision and, on Linux, the GigE receive buffer, USB3 Vision device access and where a service keeps its sessions. --json adds the build's features , the FFmpeg in use and dirs : runtime (sessions), state (presets, sign-in records), cache (FFmpeg) and inspect (previews); jpeg , the JPEG encoders and whether each hardware engine (Apple's, nvJPEG, VA-API) is on this computer and passed its accuracy check here, or why not; and hwdec , each hardware decoding method and whether it decodes here.

documents.title: Troubleshooting
documents.summary: Read error.code and error.hint first; doctor checks the computer.
documents.body: Reference Troubleshooting Read error.code and error.hint first; doctor checks the computer. capturefab doctor capturefab --json list capturefab session list capturefab -v info -c sim:0 A camera is missing or cannot connect Read the warnings of list and use the camera's full ID. For GigE, network checks reachability on its subnet. For USB3 Vision, check operating system access: doctor prints the Linux udev rule, and on Windows the camera must use WinUSB . On macOS, a camera at a correct address that reports no route to host can mean Local Network access was denied to your terminal app. camera_busy: another process holds the camera A session or another command has the camera open; error.details.held_by names it when known. Run the command through that session ( --session NAME ), wait for its job, or stop it with jobs stop or session stop . frame_timeout or trigger_timeout Make sure the camera streams and that its trigger can supply frames: info shows the trigger. Raise --timeout for slow sources, or set trigger=off . For GigE, packet loss looks like timeouts: check the receive buffer and network . A setting is locked or rejected feature_locked names the setting that locks it in details.locked_by ; change that first. Some features can change only while the camera is not streaming. set --dry-run shows what a change would write. A frame's pixel format is unsupported Choose another PixelFormat the camera offers, or capture raw to keep the bytes as they are. The pixel format table lists the supported formats. A stream, video file or encoder fails doctor shows whether FFmpeg runs. Make sure a receiving server is up and reachable. hevc and av1 need a working hardware encoder; h264 always has libx264. A development build can use CAPTUREFAB_FFMPEG=/absolute/path/to/ffmpeg . An SSH shell cannot find a session a service started Without XDG_RUNTIME_DIR , a Linux service uses /run/user/<uid> only when its user lingers. Run sudo loginctl enable-linger USER and give the service Wants= and After=user@<uid>.service . doctor in the SSH shell says where a service keeps its sessions. Capture stops with storage_full A write would have taken the disk below the free space Capturefab leaves for the system: 1% of the disk, at least 512 MiB and at most 20 GiB. error.details gives the path and its free_bytes . Free space or capture to another disk; CAPTUREFAB_MIN_FREE (bytes or a size such as 2G , 0 for none) changes the floor. Capturefab never deletes files to make room. For a bug report, include capturefab --version , the operating system, the camera type, the exact command and its JSON output, and capturefab --json doctor . Remove private addresses and names before you share them.

documents.title: Environment variables and folders
documents.summary: Variables set defaults for flags and move the folders Capturefab uses.
documents.body: Reference Environment variables and folders Variables set defaults for flags and move the folders Capturefab uses. Environment variables Variable Purpose CAPTUREFAB_JSON=1 --json for every command CAPTUREFAB_CAMERA The default -c CAPTUREFAB_SESSION The default --session ; --no-session overrides it CAPTUREFAB_KEEP The default --keep ( 60s ); 0 turns the warm default off CAPTUREFAB_CAMERA_PASSWORD The password for login add without --password-stdin CAPTUREFAB_FFMPEG An absolute path to an FFmpeg executable to use instead of the bundled one CAPTUREFAB_SESSION_DIR One folder for sessions, presets and the sign-in index; for isolated runs and tests use a private (mode 0700) folder, such as one from mktemp -d , or a path that does not exist yet CAPTUREFAB_STATE_DIR The folder for presets, the sign-in index and the jobs of ended sessions alone, such as a data partition on a read-only system CAPTUREFAB_CACHE_DIR The folder for the extracted FFmpeg, encoder probes and GenICam XML CAPTUREFAB_MIN_FREE The free space a write leaves on its disk, in bytes or a size such as 2G ; 0 turns the floor off CAPTUREFAB_THREADS At most this many image processing threads CAPTUREFAB_IMAGES How watch --show draws frames: kitty , iterm , truecolor , 256 or none CAPTUREFAB_MAX_CAMERAS Cameras one session may hold, 1–64 (default 16) CAPTUREFAB_GVSP_SCATTER=0 GigE Vision packets are received whole and copied into their frames, rather than received straight into them CAPTUREFAB_JPEG The JPEG encoder: auto (the default: Apple's JPEG engine on macOS for color frames of at least 512K pixels at the default quality, and on Linux nvJPEG or VA-API for frames of at least 512K pixels, where it is faster and as accurate as libjpeg-turbo, checked beside the first frame of each size, which libjpeg-turbo writes), cpu (libjpeg-turbo), videotoolbox , nvjpeg or vaapi ; a named engine that is missing or fails its accuracy check is exit 3. nvJPEG and VA-API run in a helper process the camera worker starts, which reads frames from the shared memory the camera wrote them to; one that crashes or stops answering is ended, and under auto libjpeg-turbo takes over, with a warning on stderr, while a named one fails the still with exit 3. CAPTUREFAB_CUDA_LIB_DIR A folder holding the CUDA runtime and nvJPEG libraries, tried before the loader's paths CAPTUREFAB_VAAPI_DEVICE The DRM render node VA-API JPEG encoding uses, instead of the first /dev/dri/renderD* that encodes JPEG CAPTUREFAB_HWDEC Hardware decoding of H.264, HEVC and other compressed video: auto (the default: compressed streams and webcams in a session, the warm one included, whose decoder runs on between commands; files and --no-session commands get their one frame sooner in software), none , or a method such as videotoolbox , cuda , vulkan or d3d11va , used for files and --no-session too; one this FFmpeg lacks or that fails its probe is exit 3. Motion JPEG is decoded with libjpeg-turbo whatever it says. A session's cameras keep the CAPTUREFAB_JPEG , CAPTUREFAB_HWDEC and CAPTUREFAB_FFMPEG the session started with, the warm auto session included: stop it with capturefab session stop auto , or use --no-session , for a command to use other values. A command's own CAPTUREFAB_MIN_FREE raises the free-space floor for the files a session writes for it, but does not lower the floor the session started with. Sessions live in the runtime folder ( $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/capturefab on Linux), presets and the sign-in index in the state folder ( ~/.local/state/capturefab on Linux; the same folder as sessions elsewhere), and the extracted FFmpeg in the cache folder. capturefab --json doctor prints all of them in dirs , and under folders the fallbacks it passed over. Where a default folder cannot be written, as on a read-only root file system, Capturefab falls back to a private folder in a tmpfs and turns off only what needs the missing folder; the embedded and read-only hosts guide lists each case.

documents.title: Build, architecture and licensing
documents.summary: One Rust executable; each camera runs in a worker process of its own, and FFmpeg runs as a separate executable.
documents.body: Reference Build, architecture and licensing One Rust executable; each camera runs in a worker process of its own, and FFmpeg runs as a separate executable. Capturefab implements GigE Vision, USB3 Vision and GenICam in Rust. Every camera command reaches its camera through a worker process, started by the command itself or held by a session, so a camera driver that hangs or crashes cannot take other cameras down. Webcams, streams, files and video encoding use the embedded FFmpeg, run as a separate process. This is an early implementation: it does not provide every feature of Aravis or vendor SDKs, and behavior can change between releases. Build from source Install a stable Rust toolchain, a C compiler and CMake, and on x86 NASM for libjpeg-turbo. Webcams, streams, files and recording need FFmpeg. A build embeds the FFmpeg named by CAPTUREFAB_FFMPEG_BINARY , or in release builds target/ffmpeg/<target>/bin/ffmpeg when it exists, which scripts/build-ffmpeg.sh builds from the pinned sources (this takes a while); cargo build never builds FFmpeg itself. At run time Capturefab uses CAPTUREFAB_FFMPEG , else the embedded copy, else an ffmpeg next to the executable or on PATH . tar -xzf capturefab-VERSION-source.tar.gz cd capturefab-VERSION cargo --config .cargo/vendor-config.toml build --release --offline --locked target/release/capturefab capture -c sim:0 -o first.png The default features are usb (USB3 Vision), jpeg (libjpeg-turbo), videotoolbox (Apple's JPEG engine on macOS), nvjpeg and vaapi (the GPU JPEG encoders on Linux, whose libraries are loaded at run time in a helper process, so a build needs no SDK), keychain (the OS credential store for login ) and shell (line editing in capturefab shell ); --no-default-features builds without them, and doctor --json lists what a build has. Licensing and release provenance Capturefab uses the MIT license. The embedded FFmpeg is GPLv3 with x264, SRT, OpenSSL and zlib; capturefab licenses prints both notices. See the FFmpeg build and compliance guide . The downloads page shows how to verify each file, and the release manifest lists files, checksums and build metadata.

documents.title: JSON results, exit codes and errors
documents.summary: Run any command with --json for one JSON document and a typed exit code.
documents.body: JSON results, exit codes and errors Run any command with --json for one JSON document and a typed exit code. --json (or CAPTUREFAB_JSON=1): one line on stdout, the result on exit 0, else {"error":{code,message,hint?,details?}}: code is the reason (see errors), the exit code its category. No nulls; warnings ≤10. snake_case keys; units in names (exposure_us); times RFC 3339 UTC; lists bounded with truncated. Credentials: never printed; URLs are redacted. capturefab schema COMMAND: arguments, result fields and errors. This page is generated from that output (contract version 1 ), so it lists exactly what the CLI accepts. Exit codes Exit code Category 0 ok 1 failed 2 usage or input 3 unavailable 4 timeout 5 unsupported 6 storage full 130 interrupted (143 SIGTERM, 129 SIGHUP) Error codes in error.code Code Exit Meaning exists 1 the output exists (never overwritten); details.path failed 1 the operation failed feature_locked 1 another setting locks the feature now; see details.locked_by incomplete 1 fewer results than requested; see details camera_ambiguous 2 several cameras match; pick one of details.candidates with -c feature_not_found 2 no such feature or control; see details.did_you_mean invalid_choice 2 not one of details.choices invalid_duration 2 not a valid duration (see grammars.duration) not_writable 2 the feature is read-only out_of_range 2 outside the feature's range; details {feature,value,min,max,inc,nearest,unit} usage 2 invalid arguments or input auth_rejected 3 the camera refused the sign-in auth_required 3 the camera needs a sign-in; run login add camera_busy 3 another process or job holds the camera; details.held_by when known camera_not_found 3 no camera matches; details.candidates lists what answered disconnected 3 the camera went away ffmpeg_missing 3 FFmpeg could not be found or started permission_denied 3 the OS refused access; see hint session_not_found 3 no running session has that name unavailable 3 the camera, stream or service cannot be reached worker_crashed 3 the camera worker process died frame_timeout 4 no frame arrived in time timeout 4 the operation did not finish in time trigger_timeout 4 a triggered camera got no trigger in time; details.trigger unsupported 5 the camera or this build cannot do that storage_full 6 disk full or below CAPTUREFAB_MIN_FREE; details {path,free_bytes?} interrupted 130 stopped by a signal; details hold partial results

repeatable --region X,Y,W,H Measure only this part of the frame: X,Y,W,H as fractions 0..1 — --preview PATH Where to write the preview (it must not exist), or none (default: a private folder doctor shows) — --size PX The preview's longest edge in pixels, 64..2048 default 768 --fresh N Frames to let pass after the first one exposed after the last settings change, 0..9 default 0 --timeout DUR How long to wait for the frame, up to 10m (default: 5s, or 3 exposures and frame periods when longer); none waits for a trigger until stopped — --warmup DUR How long a camera that sets its own exposure (a webcam, or ExposureAuto=Continuous; a network stream is already running) may take to settle after it starts; 0 measures at once default 2s --set NAME=VALUE Change settings first, as one atomic change (as set does), then measure; repeatable repeatable --for DUR Measure a frame every --every for this long (at most 50 samples), as for focusing: the series, and the sharpest frame's measurements and preview — --every DUR Time between samples with --for (default 200ms) — --clip-threshold SHARE Share of the measured pixels at full scale above which the verdict says clipped_high (default: any pixel with --region, else 0.005) — --show Draw the preview in this terminal under the measurements (kitty, iTerm2, or colour blocks) — --keep DUR Keep the camera open in a session for this long after the command, so the next one starts at once (default 60s; 0 opens and closes it in this command alone) env CAPTUREFAB_KEEP capturefab inspect -c sim:0 capturefab inspect -c sim:0 --set exposure=20ms --region 0.25,0.25,0.5,0.5 capturefab inspect -c sim:0 --keep 5m --preview none capturefab inspect -c sim:0 --show capturefab inspect JSON result Field Type and meaning after_change true — frames exposed before the camera's last settings change were let pass best {t,sharpness} — with --for: the sharpest sample camera string — camera ID cameras [{camera,frame,exposure?,verdict,suggest?,focus?,settings,preview?,after_change?,frames?,dropped?,incomplete?,resent?,warmup_ms?,settled?,warnings?,series?,best?,histogram?,channels?,region?,notes?}] — with -c repeated channels {red,green,blue} — with -v, for color dropped int — frames the transport lost meanwhile, where it counts them exposure {mean,p1,p50,p99,clipped_low,clipped_high,clipped_low_px?,clipped_high_px?,max?} — brightness 0..1; absent with --preview none region {x,y,width,height,normalized} — with -v resent int — packets the camera sent again meanwhile, where the transport counts them series [{t,sharpness,mean}] — with --for: every sample, t in seconds from the first; Effect: read . Ctrl-C ends it (exit 0). Without a terminal, or with --json, each measurement is one JSON line. capturefab watch arguments Argument or option Meaning Values -c , --camera CAM Camera: list ID, serial, IP, rtsp://…, file path, sim:0[?drop=0.02&line0=every:500ms] (default: the only one) env CAPTUREFAB_CAMERA --every DUR Time between measurements, 50ms or more default 250ms --for DUR Stop after this long (default: at Ctrl-C) — --region X,Y,W,H Measure only this part of the frame: X,Y,W,H as fractions 0..1 — --show Draw the frame in the terminal under the measurements (kitty, iTerm2, or colour blocks) — --timeout DUR How long each measurement waits for its frame, up to 10m (default: 5s, or 3 exposures and frame periods when longer) — --keep DUR Keep the camera open in a session for this long after the command, so the next one starts at once (default 60s; 0 opens and closes it in this command alone) env CAPTUREFAB_KEEP capturefab watch -c sim:0 capturefab watch -c sim:0 --show --region 0.4,0.4,0.2,0.2 capturefab watch -c sim:0 --json --for 10s --every 1s capturefab watch JSON result Field Type and meaning camera string — camera ID dropped int — frames dropped on the way exposure {mean,p1,p50,p99,clipped_low,clipped_high,…} — as inspect focus {sharpness,best,best_t} — this frame's sharpness, and the sharpest so far with its t fps float — the camera's frame rate as received, once a second of frames came frame {width,height,pixel_format,id?,age_ms} frames int — frames received since it began streaming lost int — frames lost or incomplete in transfer settings {exposure_us?,gain_db?,gain?,fps?,pixel_format?} suggest {ev,exposure_us?,limited_by?} — as inspect t float — seconds since watching began; one JSON line each --every (a terminal shows them redrawn instead) verdict [ok|dark|bright|clipped_high|clipped_low|…] — as inspect Errors: usage , failed , frame_timeout , trigger_timeout , storage_full , camera_not_found , camera_ambiguous , camera_busy , disconnected , session_not_found , unavailable , timeout . capturefab auto Settle exposure and gain, then hold them; or turn auto exposure off or on. Effect: camera_write . capturefab auto arguments Argument or option Meaning Values -c , --camera CAM Camera: list ID, serial, IP, rtsp://…, file path, sim:0[?drop=0.02&line0=every:500ms] (default: the only one) env CAPTUREFAB_CAMERA --off Turn the camera's auto exposure, gain and white balance off, keeping their values — --continuous Keep adjusting: the camera's continuous auto exposure, or Capturefab's in a session — --timeout DUR How long settling may take default 5s --region X,Y,W,H Meter only this part of the frame: X,Y,W,H as fractions 0..1 — --max-exposure DUR The longest exposure, as against motion blur: gain rises past it — --keep DUR Keep the camera open in a session for this long after the command, so the next one starts at once (default 60s; 0 opens and closes it in this command alone) env CAPTUREFAB_KEEP capturefab auto -c sim:0 capturefab auto -c sim:0 --timeout 10s capturefab auto -c sim:0 --off capturefab auto JSON result Field Type and meaning by camera|capturefab — whose auto exposure settled or runs: the camera's own (ExposureAuto Once or Continuous), or Capturefab's (with --region, --max-exposure, or when the camera has none) camera string — camera ID exposure_us float — the exposure held gain_db float — the gain held iterations int — exposure and gain changes made; by the camera, how often it was asked whether it was done job {id,camera,kind:capture|record|auto,state:armed|running|stopping|done|failed|cancelled|interrupted|lost,saved,planned?,bytes?,last_file?,next_at?,ends_at?,started,ended?,error?:{code,message}} — with --continuous by capturefab: the session job it runs as, which jobs stop ends limited_by exposure_max|exposure_min|gain_max|camera|timeout — what stopped it short of the target mean float — mean brightness 0..1 at the end mode off|continuous — with --off or --continuous settled bool — brightness reached its target, or a limit; documents.title: Presets
documents.summary: Save a camera's settings on this computer and restore them as one change.
documents.body: Presets Save a camera's settings on this computer and restore them as one change. capturefab preset Saved camera settings (host-side, portable between cameras of a model). A preset lives on this computer and can be applied to any camera of the model; a user set (exec 'UserSetSave[UserSet1]', or preset apply --persist) lives in the camera. capturefab preset save bench -c sim:0 capturefab preset apply bench -c sim:0 --dry-run capturefab preset list capturefab preset apply Restore a preset as one camera change; a failure puts every value back. Effect: camera_write . capturefab preset apply arguments Argument or option Meaning Values [NAME] — -c , --camera CAM Camera: list ID, serial, IP, rtsp://…, file path, sim:0[?drop=0.02&line0=every:500ms] (default: the only one) env CAPTUREFAB_CAMERA --file FILE Apply a preset document from a file instead of a saved preset — --dry-run Show what would change, disruptive changes included; change nothing — --strict Fail, changing nothing, if any saved value cannot be applied to this camera — --allow-other-model Apply to a camera of another model; only settings both share change — --persist USERSET Then save it in the camera's user set (default UserSet1) and make that the power-on default — --keep DUR Keep the camera open in a session for this long after the command, so the next one starts at once (default 60s; 0 opens and closes it in this command alone) env CAPTUREFAB_KEEP capturefab preset apply bench -c sim:0 --dry-run capturefab preset apply bench -c sim:0 capturefab preset apply --file bench.json -c sim:0 --strict capturefab preset apply bench -c gige:00c0df123456 --persist UserSet1 capturefab preset apply JSON result Field Type and meaning applied int — values written auto_change {current,saved,action,risk} — Capturefab auto mode auto_changed bool camera {id,vendor,model,serial} — the camera compared changes [{feature,at?,saved,current,risk:reversible|disruptive,stream_locked,warning?}] — disruptive changes may change triggering, I/O lines or acquisition rate dry_run true — with --dry-run: nothing was written match same_camera|same_model|other_model|unknown_source matched [{feature,at?,value}] not_applied [{feature,at?,status,saved,reason}] persist {user_set,default} — with --dry-run --persist: the user set it would save persisted {user_set,default} — with --persist preset string — the preset's name restarted_stream bool restarts_stream bool — a running stream stops and starts once risk reversible|disruptive — the whole change unchanged int — values that already match warnings [string] Errors: usage , failed , unsupported , out_of_range , invalid_choice , not_writable , feature_locked , camera_not_found , camera_busy , unavailable , timeout . capturefab preset export Write a preset's document to a file, or to stdout. Effect: file_write . capturefab preset export arguments Argument or option Meaning Values NAME — -o , --output FILE The file to write; it must not exist — capturefab preset export bench -o bench.json capturefab preset export bench > bench.json capturefab preset export JSON result Field Type and meaning auto {balance} — without -o camera {transport,vendor,model,serial?,kind} — without -o name string — without -o note string — without -o path string — with -o: the file written preset string — with -o: the preset's name saved_at string — without -o skipped [{feature,at?,reason}] — without -o values [{feature,value,at?:[{selector,value}]}] — without -o version int — without -o: the document itself, as preset show prints it Errors: usage , failed , exists , storage_full , camera_not_found , unsupported . capturefab preset import Save a preset document from a file, such as one preset export wrote. Effect: file_write . capturefab preset import arguments Argument or option Meaning Values FILE — --name NAME Save it under this name instead of the one in the file — --replace Overwrite a saved preset with the same name — capturefab preset import bench.json capturefab preset import bench.json --name bench2 capturefab preset import JSON result Field Type and meaning camera string — the camera read (save) preset {name,camera,values,skipped,saved_at,path} — values is a count Errors: usage , failed , exists , storage_full , camera_not_found , unsupported . capturefab preset list List saved presets and the folder that holds them. Effect: read . capturefab preset list capturefab --json preset list capturefab preset list JSON result Field Type and meaning dir string — the folder that holds presets presets [{name,transport?,vendor,model,serial?,saved_at,values,note?,status?:unreadable|newer_version,reason?}] — values is a count Errors: usage , failed , camera_not_found , camera_ambiguous , camera_busy , permission_denied , disconnected , auth_required , auth_rejected , session_not_found , ffmpeg_missing , unavailable , timeout . capturefab preset rm Delete a saved preset; no camera changes. Effect: file_write . capturefab preset rm arguments Argument or option Meaning Values NAME — capturefab preset rm bench capturefab --json preset rm bench capturefab preset rm JSON result Field Type and meaning removed string — the preset's name Errors: usage , failed , camera_not_found , camera_ambiguous , camera_busy , permission_denied , disconnected , auth_required , auth_rejected , session_not_found , ffmpeg_missing , unavailable , timeout . capturefab preset save Save the camera's current settings as a named preset. Effect: file_write . capturefab preset save arguments Argument or option Meaning Values NAME — -c , --camera CAM Camera: list ID, serial, IP, rtsp://…, file path, sim:0[?drop=0.02&line0=every:500ms] (default: the only one) env CAPTUREFAB_CAMERA --note NOTE A short note, such as the lighting it was tuned for — --replace Overwrite a saved preset with the same name — --keep DUR Keep the camera open in a session for this long after the command, so the next one starts at once (default 60s; 0 opens and closes it in this command alone) env CAPTUREFAB_KEEP capturefab preset save bench -c sim:0 capturefab preset save line1 -c gige:00c0df123456 --note 'ring light 60%' capturefab preset save JSON result Field Type and meaning camera string — the camera read (save) preset {name,camera,values,skipped,saved_at,path} — values is a count Errors: usage , failed , exists , storage_full , camera_not_found , unsupported . capturefab preset show Show a saved preset's values. documents.title: Sessions and jobs
documents.summary: Keep cameras open between commands and run captures and recordings in the background.
documents.body: Sessions and jobs Keep cameras open between commands and run captures and recordings in the background. capturefab session Sessions keep cameras open between commands: start one in the background, stop it, see it. Camera commands keep their camera open in the auto session for 60s after their last use (--keep DUR to change it, --keep 0 or --no-session for none), and use a session that holds their camera on their own. capturefab session start -c sim:0 --live capturefab session status capturefab session stop capturefab session list The running sessions. Effect: read . capturefab session list capturefab --json session list capturefab session list JSON result Field Type and meaning sessions [{session,pid,uptime_s,cameras:[string]}] Errors: usage , failed , session_not_found , unavailable , timeout . capturefab session start Start a session in the background; it ends after --idle unused. Effect: disruptive . capturefab session start arguments Argument or option Meaning Values --name NAME Session name other commands pass to --session default default -c , --camera CAM Camera, repeatable: list ID, serial, IP, rtsp://…, file path, sim:0[?drop=0.02&line0=every:500ms] (default: the only one) env CAPTUREFAB_CAMERA ; repeatable --live Keep the cameras streaming, so captures take the newest frame at once — --idle DUR End after this long with no requests and no running jobs default 30m capturefab session start -c sim:0 capturefab session start --name line1 -c gige:00c0df123456 --live --idle 8h capturefab session start JSON result Field Type and meaning cameras [string] — camera IDs it holds log string — where its output goes pid int session string — its name, for --session started bool — false when it was already running warnings [string] Errors: usage , failed , camera_not_found , camera_busy , auth_required , auth_rejected , unavailable , invalid_duration , timeout . capturefab session status A session's cameras, their state and jobs. Effect: read . capturefab session status arguments Argument or option Meaning Values [NAME] The session (default: the only one running) — capturefab session status capturefab --json session status line1 capturefab session status JSON result Field Type and meaning cameras [{id,state:idle|streaming|recording|error,error?:{code,message,hint?,details?:{exit?,signal?,stderr_tail?}},last_error?,config_state?:unknown,frames?,dropped?,lost?,incomplete?,resent?,fps?,jobs:[job]}] — job as jobs lists it; fps: the rate frames arrive at while it streams, by the camera's clock where it stamps them; error: the camera's worker exited (code worker_crashed, with its exit status or signal and last lines of stderr) or did not answer, and the next command on the camera starts another; last_error: the worker's last logged error; lost: frames lost on the way, incomplete: frames the transport received incomplete, resent: packets the camera sent again, where it can tell; config_state unknown: it exited during a settings change, until settings are written again pid int session string uptime_s int Errors: usage , failed , session_not_found , unavailable , timeout . capturefab session stop Stop a session once its recordings and captures are finished. Effect: disruptive . capturefab session stop arguments Argument or option Meaning Values [NAME] The session (default: the only one running) — capturefab session stop capturefab session stop line1 capturefab session stop JSON result Field Type and meaning pid int session string stopped bool — true once the process has exited Errors: usage , failed , session_not_found , unavailable , timeout . capturefab serve Run a session in the foreground (systemd, a terminal); Ctrl-C stops it. documents.body: Sign-ins and networks Save camera passwords, resolve ONVIF streams and check GigE paths. capturefab login Save camera sign-ins for rtsp:// and ONVIF cameras in the OS credential store. printf '%s\n' "$PASS" | capturefab login add rtsp://cam.local/stream --user admin --password-stdin capturefab login list capturefab login rm rtsp://cam.local/stream capturefab login add Check a camera sign-in, then save it in the OS credential store.
